To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the glutamoylation of curcumin improves the neuroprotective effects of curcumin in Parkinson’s disease.

glutamoyl curcuminate (a glutamoyl ester of curcumin) offers improved protection against PN-mediated nitration of brain mitochondrial proteins and inhibition of mitochondrial complex I (a major enzyme complex involved in energy generation) compared to the native form of curcumin.
di-glutamyol curcumin could protect against peroxynirtrite-induced nitrosative stress in mitochondria and could protect against 1-methlyl-4-phenylyridinium (MMP+) toxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of improved antioxidants for the treatment of PD.
the development of a curcumin-based neuroprotective agent against PD.
the identification of a novel glutamoyl conjugate of curcumin as a potent neuroprotective agent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
di-glutamate ester of curcumin offers better protection against PN-mediated nitro-oxidative stress and damage to brain mitochondria in comparison to curcumin.

di-glutamate curcumin could protect brain mitochondria and dopaminergic neurons in vitro against PN-mediated damage and therefore could be a potential therapeutic agent for neurodegenerative disorders.
the di-glutamyl conjugate of curcumin offers better neuroprotection against nitrosative stress-induced mitochondrial damage compared to the parent curcumin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
di-glutamate curcumin is a better candidate than curcumin for the development of a neuroprotective drug in PD.
di-glutamylation of curcumin improves the antioxidant properties of curcumin and could be a better therapeutic agent for PD.
di-glutamate ester of curcumin could offer improved protection against PN-mediated mitochondrial dysfunction in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bioconjugated form of curcumin could provide improved therapeutic value in PD.
the di-glutamyl conjugate of curcumin offers a better protection against PN-dependent mitochondrial dysfunction and protein nitration than other bioconjugates.
the glutamoylated diester of curicumin is a more potent neuroprotective agent than curcumin itself and may be useful for the treatment of PD.
